bases.name: Grove (Jutland)
bases.note: The file's jump-off airfield: 775 km to Scapa Flow with the 300-litre tank on the Bf 109 (great circle about 780 km).

bases.name: Stavanger-Sola (Norway)
bases.note: The file names Stavanger-Scapa Flow as 510 km, too far for fighter escort; its map shows Sola among the jump-off airfields (great circle about 500 km).

bases.name: Tirstrup (Jutland)
bases.note: Where Beeger was to direct the operation in February 1945 (CSDIC report). About 865 km to Scapa Flow: beyond the 750–800 km of the Mistel of 1944, within the 1,500 km of the Mistel of 1945.

windows.label: Late May 1944, with what is ready
windows.availableNote: Assumption: of the 15 combinations, the 2 prototypes plus the 13 due by 15 June completed at an even rate from 18 April.

windows.label: After 15 June 1944, on the file's schedule
windows.availableNote: The file: 15 Mistel in all, the remaining 13 complete about 15 June.

windows.label: February 1945: Dragon's Lair
windows.availableNote: Assumption: the number set aside for Dragon's Lair is not in any document found; the study lets it equal the file of 1944. The war diary counts 130 Mistel built or under construction on 2 February 1945, most of them meant for Eisenhammer.

shipsNote: Presence: the share of days each heavy ship spent at Scapa in the fifteen days round the date (13–27 May, 13–27 June 1944; all of February 1945), from the war diary of the Commander-in-Chief, Home Fleet (Admiralty war diaries, ADM 199, as transcribed by Don Kindell on naval-history.net). Battleships and fleet carriers only; escort carriers, cruisers and destroyers are not counted, as the file did not count them.

assumptionNotes.serviceable: Share of combinations that take off. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.reconSuccess: Chance that the reconnaissance flight the file demands brings back usable photographs of the anchorage. Assumption; the file only says reconnaissance must come first.
assumptionNotes.interceptDay: Share of combinations lost to fighters on the way in, in daylight at very low level (the study's method). Assumption; the file expects 160–200 fighters and a radar belt 'without gaps'.
assumptionNotes.interceptDawn: The same for the night flight arriving at dawn (the covering memo's method). Assumption.
assumptionNotes.interceptFeb: The same in February 1945, whatever the method. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.findSchwan: Chance of reaching the anchorage with the 'Schwan' buoy and the 'Sonne' beacon, as the file proposes. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.findDawn: The same at night and dawn. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.findWinter: The same in February 1945, with winter winds. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.identifyFresh: Chance of steering straight for a ship with fresh photographs, as the file demands. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.identifyOld: The same with the old target dossiers of 1939–41 only. Assumption; the file says crews cannot pick out targets on arrival.
assumptionNotes.flakLoss: Share lost to the anchorage's anti-aircraft fire in the pull-up and glide (release at 700 m, 2 km from the target, after the file). Assumption.
assumptionNotes.hit: Chance that a released Ju 88 strikes the ship it is aimed at. Assumption; the file gives only the scatter (18 × 18 m) and reckons that one hit destroys a battleship.
assumptionNotes.sinkBB: Chance that a hit sinks a battleship rather than damaging it. Assumption; the file expects destruction by one hit.
assumptionNotes.sinkCV: The same for a fleet carrier. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.returnGrove: Chance that a fighter pilot gets back to Jutland after 775 km out and the attack. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.returnSola: The same from Stavanger, 510 km. Assumption.
assumptionNotes.returnTirstrup: The same in February 1945 (later accounts say the pilots were to land in Norway). Assumption.
assumptionNotes.solaAlert: Added interception if the combinations are first moved to Norway, where British reconnaissance and the code-breakers could see them. Assumption.

weatherNote: Chance that the weather on the planned days allows the low flight and the attack. Assumptions: 75 % for May–June, 45 % for February. Beeger said bad weather made them abandon the operation in February 1945.

royalOak.cite: Roskill, The War at Sea, vol. I (1954), p. 74: 'Twenty-four officers and 809 men of her complement perished.'
